text: Dans un match palpitant de la Northbridge League, Seabrook Town a battu Harbour City 4-2 grâce à une seconde mi-temps explosive. Marek Barros, élu meilleur joueur avec une note parfaite de 10, a ouvert le score pour Harbour City juste après la pause[#975]. Mais c’est Seabrook Town qui a dominé ensuite, en inscrivant 4 buts grâce à leur style de jeu direct et agressif. Ils ont appuyé leur victoire sur une pressions plus intense et des contre-attaques rapides[#1361]. Notamment, Kian Romano a marqué deux buts décisifs en fin de match avec de très bonnes occasions, ce qui a fait basculer le score[#1882][#1906]. Harbour City a souffert après l’expulsion de Joon Whitfield en première période[#871], et leur jeu posé n’a pas suffi à contenir l’énergie de Seabrook.

trace.output: Brief: full-match recap for fan audience in fr

- Seabrook Town's tactical shift around the 65th minute involved pressing higher, playing more direct, and pushing their defensive line further up. This change reflects a more aggressive approach to chase the game, increasing press intensity by 0.84, directness by 0.57, and line height by 0.72. This likely helped them regain possession quickly and exploit spaces from turnovers, consistent with their 3-4-3 formation designed to facilitate wide, crossing play and quick transitions [1361].
- Seabrook Town's goals in the second half stemmed from regains and quick build-ups with relatively few passes and short durations (e.g., Tariq Marlowe's goal following a regain with no passes; Callum Varga's goal following a 3-pass move after a regain). This indicates effective counter-attacking triggered by pressing and regaining the ball high up the pitch, exploiting Harbour City's 4-2-3-1 formation's patient, short passing style which could be vulnerable to quick turnovers [1104,1448].
- Harbour City’s goals came through more patient build-up: Elias Okafor’s equalizer resulted from a long 56.9s sequence with 17 passes, emphasizing their patient short-passing style from their 4-2-3-1 setup. Marek Barros’s goal originated from a corner cross, showing use of set pieces to create chances, which fits with their possession-focused, less direct approach [905,975].
- In the late stages, Seabrook Town capitalized on turnovers leading to a rapid counter-attack resulting in Kian Romano's equalizing goal at 90+2', assisted by a through ball, aligning with their increased directness and pressing. Harbour City responded by adopting a higher press and more direct play themselves, indicating a shift from their usual patient style to chase the game [1882,1884].

- Seabrook Town won with a final score of 4-2 against Harbour City [#final_score].
- Marek Barros (Harbour City) scored at 47' with an xG of 0.029 and was named player of the match with a rating of 10.0 [#975].
- Seabrook Town scored 4 goals in the second half, supported by a higher xG of 2.76 compared to Harbour City's 0.25 [#second_half].
- Kian Romano scored two late goals at 90+2' and 90+3', with high xG values of 0.554 and 0.994 respectively, shifting the lead to Seabrook Town [#1882, #1906].
- Harbour City received a red card for Joon Whitfield at 43' which likely impacted their game [#871].
